# HLF Pulse — Verified New Zealand Mortgage, Housing, KiwiSaver & Protection Reference Dataset

> Public reference dataset and data dictionary built 100% live from official New Zealand Crown, statutory, and industry releases, with clearly labelled HLF-derived calculations and interpretation.
> Created by: Andy Palliser (Andrew Jonathan Palliser, FSP1004725), Mortgage & KiwiSaver Adviser · Home Loan Factory (https://www.homeloanfactory.co.nz/team/andrew-palliser) | Published by: Home Loan Factory (https://www.homeloanfactory.co.nz/).
> Media Kit & Citation Guide: https://www.homeloanfactory.co.nz/media-and-citations | HLF Glossary: https://www.homeloanfactory.co.nz/tools/glossary
> Reuse Licence: CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/) for HLF-derived figures & commentary; official statistics credited to their respective publishers.
> Date Standard: Observation Period (latest monthly: September 2026) | Period End | Source Publication Date | Last Checked (14 November 2026 / 2026-11-14).
> Active datasets: 69.

## Machine-Readable Endpoints
- Structured Data Dictionary & Records (JSON): https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/pulse.json
- Webflow Chat Bubble Feed (JSON): https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/nz-mortgage-pulse.json
- Main Reference Dataset Hub (HTML): https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/
- Media Kit & Citation Guide (HTML): https://www.homeloanfactory.co.nz/media-and-citations

## Canonical Data Dictionary Records (69 Active Datasets)
- [ACC Earners' Levy rate, Maximum Liable Earnings cap & 80% weekly compensation ceiling (Obs: 2026/27 Tax Year (from 1 April 2026) | End: 2026-04-30 | Published: 2026-04-01 (1 April 2026 — 2026/27 ACC Earners' Levy schedule effective date))](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/acc-earners-levy-cap/): For the 2026/27 tax year, the ACC Earners' Levy is $1.75 per $100 (1.75% incl. GST) up to a Maximum Liable Earnings cap of $156,641 (a maximum annual levy of $2,741.22), capping ACC's 80% weekly compensation at $125,312.80/year ($2,409.86/week gross). [Official Data: ACC / IRD 2026/27 Statutory Schedule: Earners' levy = $1.75 per $100 incl. GST ($1.52 excl. GST); Maximum liable earnings = $156,641 (vs $152,790 in 2025/26). | HLF Calculation: Max Levy: ($156,641 ÷ 100) × $1.75 = $2,741.22/yr | Max 80% Comp: $156,641 × 80% = $125,312.80/yr ($2,409.86/wk) | Derived by HLF Pulse: Yes | Cite as: HLF Pulse, Home Loan Factory. "ACC Earners' Levy rate, Maximum Liable Earnings cap & 80% weekly compensation ceiling," 2026/27 Tax Year (from 1 April 2026). Derived by HLF from Accident Compensation Corporation (ACC) & Inland Revenue — Earners' Levy Statutory Schedule. https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/acc-earners-levy-cap/ (checked 14 November 2026). CC BY 4.0.]
- [ACC annual accepted injury claims vs new weekly income compensation claims (Obs: 2025/26 ACC Financial Year | End: 2026-06-30 | Published: 2026-10-29 (29 October 2026 — ACC Annual Report 2025/26 release))](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/acc-weekly-compensation-claims/): In 2025/26, ACC registered over 2,100,000 accepted injury claims across New Zealand (mostly minor treatment-only visits) and 105,000 new weekly income compensation claims for time off work (down 1.9% from 107,000 in 2024/25, or 5.0 weekly compensation claims per 100 accepted injury claims). [Official Data: ACC Annual Report (2025/26): Total accepted injury claims = 2,100,000+ (+1.6% YoY, including minor treatment-only claims); New weekly compensation entitlement claims = 105,000 (-1.9% from 107,000 in 2024/25). | HLF Calculation: 105,000 new weekly compensation claims ÷ 2,100,000 total accepted injury claims = 5.0 per 100 accepted claims (separate annual claim counts) | Derived by HLF Pulse: Yes | Cite as: HLF Pulse, Home Loan Factory. "ACC annual accepted injury claims vs new weekly income compensation claims," 2025/26 ACC Financial Year. Derived by HLF from Accident Compensation Corporation (ACC) — Annual Report & Official Claim Statistics. https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/acc-weekly-compensation-claims/ (checked 14 November 2026). CC BY 4.0.]
- [Average gross borrower income for approved first-home buyers vs property investors (Obs: September 2026 | End: 2026-09-30 | Published: 2026-10-27 (27 October 2026))](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/borrower-income/): In September 2026, approved New Zealand first-home buyer mortgage applications averaged $144,232 in gross borrower income (ranging from $123,000 to $197,000 across DTI bands). [Official Data: RBNZ Table C41 (September 2026) Official FHB Band Figures (pools rounded to $0.1m, averages to $1,000): TDTI ≤ 3x income: $197,000 avg ($59.0m pool / 299.5 implied apps) | 3x < TDTI ≤ 4x income: $151,000 avg ($101.0m pool / 668.9 implied apps) | 4x < TDTI ≤ 5x income: $139,000 avg ($124.0m pool / 892.1 implied apps) | 5x < TDTI ≤ 6x income: $125,000 avg ($76.0m pool / 608.0 implied apps) | TDTI > 6x income: $123,000 avg ($23.0m pool / 187.0 implied apps). | HLF Calculation: FHB: $383.0m total band income ÷ 2,655.4 implied applications = $144,232 (subject to RBNZ band rounding) | Derived by HLF Pulse: Yes | Cite as: HLF Pulse, Home Loan Factory. "Average gross borrower income for approved first-home buyers vs property investors," September 2026. Derived by HLF from Reserve Bank of New Zealand — Residential mortgage borrower gross income (BGI) (Table C41). https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/borrower-income/ (checked 14 November 2026). CC BY 4.0.]
- [Annual change in the cost of purchasing a newly built home (CPI) (Obs: September 2026 quarter | End: 2026-09-30 | Published: Quarterly Stats NZ CPI release (~3 weeks after reference quarter-end))](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/build-cost-inflation/): In the September 2026 quarter, the cost of purchasing a newly built home changed by +3.2% year-on-year, compared with 3.7% headline CPI inflation. [Official Data: Stats NZ CPI (September 2026 quarter): Purchase of newly built home = +3.2% YoY. | HLF Calculation: Directly reported Stats NZ CPI purchase of new housing = +3.2% YoY | Derived by HLF Pulse: No (Officially reported) | Cite as: HLF Pulse, Home Loan Factory. "Annual change in the cost of purchasing a newly built home (CPI)," September 2026 quarter. Source: Stats NZ — Consumers Price Index (Purchase of new housing sub-index). https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/build-cost-inflation/ (checked 14 November 2026). CC BY 4.0.]
- [Annual residential dwelling (building) insurance price index inflation (Stats NZ CPI) (Obs: September 2026 quarter | End: 2026-09-30 | Published: Quarterly Stats NZ CPI release (~3 weeks after quarter-end))](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/building-insurance-inflation/): In the September 2026 quarter, residential dwelling (building) insurance prices rose +14.6% year-on-year—sitting +11.4 percentage points above headline CPI inflation (3.2%). [Official Data: Stats NZ CPI (September 2026 quarter): Dwelling insurance price index = +14.6% YoY; All-groups CPI = +3.2% YoY. | HLF Calculation: Dwelling insurance CPI (+14.6%) minus All-groups CPI (+3.2%) = +11.4 percentage points (CPI measures index price change, not dollar premiums) | Derived by HLF Pulse: No (Officially reported) | Cite as: HLF Pulse, Home Loan Factory. "Annual residential dwelling (building) insurance price index inflation (Stats NZ CPI)," September 2026 quarter. Source: Stats NZ — Consumers Price Index (Dwelling insurance sub-index). https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/building-insurance-inflation/ (checked 14 November 2026). CC BY 4.0.]
- [Total New Zealand personal & consumer lending stock across banks & non-bank lenders (RBNZ Table C5) (Obs: September 2026 | End: 2026-09-30 | Published: Monthly RBNZ statistical release (~4 weeks after reference month-end))](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/consumer-personal-lending-stock/): As at September 2026, total New Zealand personal and consumer lending (personal loans, vehicle finance, hire purchase, overdrafts, and cards) stood at $14.64B ($14,636m) (up 2.2% year-on-year from $14.32B a year earlier), including $7.33B (50.1%) from non-bank lenders. [Official Data: RBNZ Table C5 (September 2026): Total consumer sector lending stock = $14,636m ($14.64B). | HLF Calculation: Total NZ Consumer Lending = $14,636m ($14.64B; YoY: +2.2%) | Non-Bank Share: $7,332m ÷ $14,636m = 50.1% | Derived by HLF Pulse: Yes | Cite as: HLF Pulse, Home Loan Factory. "Total New Zealand personal & consumer lending stock across banks & non-bank lenders (RBNZ Table C5)," September 2026. Derived by HLF from Reserve Bank of New Zealand — Sector lending (Table C5). https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/consumer-personal-lending-stock/ (checked 14 November 2026). CC BY 4.0.]

- [New Zealand credit card debt, share accruing interest & weighted average interest rate (RBNZ Table C12) (Obs: August 2026 | End: 2026-08-31 | Published: Monthly RBNZ statistical release (~4 weeks after reference month-end))](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/credit-card-balances-interest-share/): In August 2026, New Zealanders owed $5.38B ($5,378m) in credit card balances (down 1.9% year-on-year from $5,481m a year earlier), with 51.3% ($2,758m) accruing interest at a weighted average rate of 20.0% p.a.. [Official Data: RBNZ Table C12 (August 2026): Total credit card advances outstanding = $5,378m ($5.38B). | HLF Calculation: Total Card Advances = $5,378m ($5.38B) | Interest-Bearing: $2,758m ÷ $5,378m = 51.3% at 20.0% p.a. | Derived by HLF Pulse: Yes | Cite as: HLF Pulse, Home Loan Factory. - [First-home buyer high Debt-to-Income (>6x DTI) share vs 20% RBNZ speed limit (Obs: September 2026 | End: 2026-09-30 | Published: 2026-10-27 (27 October 2026))](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/dti-headroom/): In September 2026, 9.1% of first-home buyer mortgage lending had a Debt-to-Income (DTI) ratio above 6x ($139.0m of $1,527.0m)—sitting 10.9 percentage points below the 20% RBNZ speed-limit cap. [Official Data: RBNZ Table C40 (September 2026): FHB lending with TDTI > 6 = $139.0m out of $1,527.0m total FHB commitments. | HLF Calculation: $139.0m ÷ $1,527.0m = 9.1% (Benchmark diff: 20.0% - 9.1% = 10.9 pts) | Derived by HLF Pulse: Yes | Cite as: HLF Pulse, Home Loan Factory. [Official Data: RBNZ Table C31 (September 2026): 1,325 <=80% LVR FHB borrowers ($680m) out of 2,667 total FHB borrowers. | HLF Calculation: 1,325 ÷ 2,667 = 49.7% (Mean loan: $680m × $1m ÷ 1,325 = $513,208) | Derived by HLF Pulse: Yes | Cite as: HLF Pulse, Home Loan Factory. [Official Data: RBNZ Table C31 (12 months to September 2026): Sum of monthly FHB approvals = 33,485 loans ($19,613m); >80% LVR FHB approvals = 15,743 loans. | HLF Calculation: 12-month sum = 33,485 loans ($19,613m); >80% LVR share = 15,743 ÷ 33,485 = 47.0% | Derived by HLF Pulse: Yes | Cite as: HLF Pulse, Home Loan Factory. - [Median New Zealand student loan balance (Inland Revenue) (Obs: June 2026 | End: 2026-06-30 | Published: Quarterly Inland Revenue Student Loan statistics release (~6 weeks after quarter-end))](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/student-loan-servicing/): As at June 2026, the median New Zealand student loan balance was $18,301 (up 4.5% on a year earlier from $17,516 in June 2025). [Official Data: Inland Revenue Student Loan Scheme (June 2026): Median borrower balance = $18,301 (compared with $17,516 in June 2025). | HLF Calculation: Reported IRD median = $18,301 (Change: ($18,301 - $17,516) ÷ $17,516 = +4.5%) | Derived by HLF Pulse: No (Officially reported) | Cite as: HLF Pulse, Home Loan Factory. "Median New Zealand student loan balance (Inland Revenue)," June 2026. - [Mortgage top-up share of approvals & average top-up amount (Obs: September 2026 | End: 2026-09-30 | Published: 2026-10-27 (27 October 2026))](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/top-ups/): In September 2026, 9,639 homeowners were approved for a mortgage top-up on their existing property—accounting for 46.4% of all mortgage approvals across New Zealand, with an average top-up of $99,803. [Official Data: RBNZ Table C33 (September 2026): Top-up approvals = 9,639 borrowers ($962m) out of 20,763 total approvals. | HLF Calculation: 9,639 ÷ 20,763 = 46.4% (Mean top-up: $962m × $1m ÷ 9,639 = $99,803) | Derived by HLF Pulse: Yes | Cite as: HLF Pulse, Home Loan Factory. "Mortgage top-up share of approvals & average top-up amount," September 2026. Derived by HLF from Reserve Bank of New Zealand — New residential mortgage lending by purpose (Table C33). https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/top-ups/ (checked 14 November 2026). CC BY 4.0.]

- [Multi-unit & townhouse share of new residential dwelling consents (Obs: September 2026 | End: 2026-09-30 | Published: Monthly Stats NZ Building Consents release (~4 weeks after reference month-end))](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/townhouse-share/): In September 2026, 51.5% (1,837 of 3,570) of new residential dwelling consents were for multi-unit homes—with townhouses, flats, and units accounting for 36.6% (1,305) and apartments plus retirement village units accounting for 14.9% (532). [Official Data: Stats NZ Building Consents (September 2026): Total dwellings = 3,570; Stand-alone houses = 1,733; Townhouses, flats & units = 1,305; Apartments & retirement units = 532. | HLF Calculation: Multi-unit overall: (3,570 − 1,733) ÷ 3,570 = 1,837 ÷ 3,570 = 51.5% | Townhouses/flats/units: 1,305 ÷ 3,570 = 36.6% | Derived by HLF Pulse: Yes | Cite as: HLF Pulse, Home Loan Factory. "Multi-unit & townhouse share of new residential dwelling consents," September 2026. Derived by HLF from Stats NZ — Building Consents Issued (Monthly Information Release). https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/townhouse-share/ (checked 14 November 2026). CC BY 4.0.]
- [Annual motor vehicle insurance price index inflation (Stats NZ CPI) (Obs: September 2026 quarter | End: 2026-09-30 | Published: Quarterly Stats NZ CPI release (~3 weeks after quarter-end))](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/vehicle-insurance-inflation/): In the September 2026 quarter, motor vehicle insurance prices rose +8.8% year-on-year—sitting +5.6 percentage points above headline CPI (+3.2%). [Official Data: Stats NZ CPI (September 2026 quarter): Vehicle insurance price index = +8.8% YoY; All-groups CPI = +3.2% YoY. | HLF Calculation: Vehicle insurance CPI (+8.8%) minus All-groups CPI (+3.2%) = +5.6 percentage points | Derived by HLF Pulse: No (Officially reported) | Cite as: HLF Pulse, Home Loan Factory.
